key_insight: PEA organic spacers slow degradation and improve ambient light and thermal stability relative to BA spacers in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires defect control, surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 nanoflakes under ambient light and thermal stress.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
Examined spacer-dependent morphology, lattice defects and decomposition.
evidence_signal: Fresh nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals exhibited better morphology, fewer lattice defects and slower degradation despite shared decomposition pathways to PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or device-level photovoltaic testing, so improved material durability does not establish longer solar-cell lifetime.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
